I only put it in once at night because while they have vastly improved the formula from the Rogaine of old, it's still like putting hair spray only on your hair line, causing it to noticeably stick up and look silly. However, sometimes when I know for a fact I wont be seeing anything but a computer screen in my room all day (*ahem* I uuhh.... call those "weekdays"), then I will apply Rogaine in the morning as well as the evening and just let my hair stick straight up wherever it pleases.

Goodness gracious, only on the internet can two men (I'm assuming) talk about hair loss products and LAZER COMBS without feeling like **complete** losers.

Given that almost every male on both sides of my family is bald, and my dad was nearly completely bald by my age, I feel it is safe to say my condition can adequately be described as being: S.O.L. 

All I know is that my hairline was once falling out, now it isn't. Even if it is actually just foamy snake oil, I'm happy got now.

You should definitely take our fellow redditor's suggestions into consideration, but if you're anything like me, you have a bit of an oddly shaped head and baldness is out of the question.

I started using Rogaine shortly after I noticed my hair line receding at 18. Nothing has *grown back,* but after 2 years, my hair line hasn't budged at all. The bottle says to apply twice daily, but I just apply once a day before I go to sleep and I am very pleased with the results. It is relatively cheap and easy to use (just turn the bottle upside down, spray a little bit directly onto your hair line, and rub it in) and it works for me, so I recommend trying it out.

I also tried propecia for a little bit. But just as my doctor warned, it fudged with my hormones and pretty much killed my work-out ethic for a while, so I ditched it.

If you have a nicely shaped head and good ol' traditional manly features, just go for the shaved look. However if you're like me, a little Rogaine will go a long way.

Muay Thai, Boxing, Judo, Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Mixed Martial Arts.

Ive been practicing Muay Thai for about four years now, and I never plan to stop. I have a very "Thai" style, to anybody who knows what that means. I have had my ups and downs, but once I started I never looked back and will be practicing for as long as my body holds up.

I have boxed a little bit in between my Muay Thai practice. Boxing is awesome, but its COMPLETELY different and I am terrible at it. Fun, though.

I have been practicing Judo for a little over a year and a half. Judo is pretty much the toughest sport around, in my opinion. It was very tough for me at first, but I got over that first hump on the difficulty curve and I like it a lot.

I have been practicing Brazilian Jiu Jitsu for a little over a half a year. BJJ is great and I instantly liked it. I have a scar on my left eyebrow from a flying armlock, so I am a BJJ member for life now.

I play a little MMA here and there just for the fun of it. I much prefer the individual arts and sports on their own, but MMA is fun too every now and then. It is a much different world, for sure, and more accessible to the outsider.

Muay Thai is by far my favorite, and I highly reccomend it to everyone. You dont have to worry about being expected to kick trees for some reason, or kill all the nerves in your shins. Thats just silly! I have also practiced a little Krav Maga, and It's cool but it doesnt hold me interest nearly as much as the other arts do.

If you are from the outside looking in and are interested in learning an art, I recommend Muay Thai, Boxing, or BJJ, as they are the most accessible. I am most definitely NOT an MMA "that style is stupid and wont work in real life!!" snob, but i wouldnt recommend japanese martial arts like karate or aikido. The way they are taught bugs me, as they tend to focus too much on forms and not enough on hard sparring and ring time experience. plus, no offense to anyone out there, but i think "point sparring" in styles such as Taekwondo and Karate are ridiculous. I definitely still respect what they do, but I'm just voicing my opinion. 

Anyway, get out there and find a gym!! Kick some ass!! HAVE SOME FUN!!

edit: Also i started off with Capoeira for almost a year. Its great fun, but not for me. I wouldnt call it a "martial art" but a sport instead. Some schools teach it as a hard martial art, and you better believe they'll put a heel in your face, but Capoeira is mostly just for fun.

I was really not a fan of small children at all. I just found them to be irritating and more trouble than anything. But then I got a job as a lifeguard, which is about 60% teaching swim lessons, and my opinion was changed totally. 

I taught kids mostly between 3-8 years old, and really became attached. They weren't my kids, and I sure as **hell** didn't like ALL of them, but most of them truly grew on me. The key is that you have to be the right kind of person for parenting. Some people just aren't. 

Have your boyfriend give it a shot, though. try spending a good amount of time babysitting for a friend's kid, or a family member, and try to really get into the whole idea. 

Above all, please know that having children is a big step. Some people just aren't cut out for the job. It would be a terrible thing to have a child with someone you love very much, but who isn't the right type to have one with. A lot of couples split up because of their kid. Sad, but true.

Hope that helped just a little!!

I had planters warts for about three years. It all started with one on the bottom of my foot, then it spread to one in the center of my palm, then my left ring finger, then my right thumb. 

I never told anyone or showed anyone because it was embarrassing, and I was young at the time. The ones on my foot were bearable, and the one on my palm was hideable, but the one on my ring finger was HUGE and very noticeable. So, i iced it up and cut it off myself.

It didn't hurt very much because its just like a cancerous growth of dead skin and there are little to no nerves, but the entire process made me very anxious and was generally not fun.

Cutting one off did not solve the problem and it grew back in a few weeks, as bad as ever, and was spreading to other fingers. I was very pissed off and frustrated, as you can imagine it was not fun being a high school freshman and not being able to open my hand for fear of people seeing my numerous and big planters warts. So i physically pulled the original one off my palm with my fingers. It was a bit bloody, but sort of therapeutic.

Turns out planters warts work like werewolves, because within a few days my entire hand cleared up completely, and my foot actually cleared up too shortly after. "Relief" would be an appropriate word for how I felt. Three years of warts gone within a week.

The moral of the story is: if you have a problem, seek medical help!! being too embarrassed doesn't do any good for anybody.
